about: The evangelium of the formulary “Low Sunday” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, when it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors of the place where the disciples were gathered were shut for fear of the Jews, Jesus came, stood among them, and said to them: Peace be with you. After saying this, He showed them His hands and His side. So the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord. He therefore said to them again: Peace be with you. Just as the Father sent Me, I also send you. After saying this, He breathed and said to them: Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive anyone’s sins, those sins are forgiven; and if you retain anyone’s sins, those sins remain retained. Thomas, however, one of the twelve, who is called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. So the other disciples said to him: We have seen the Lord. But he said to them: Unless I see the mark of the nails in His hands and put my finger where the nails were and put my hand into His side, I will not believe. And after eight days His disciples were indoors again, and Thomas was with them. While the doors were shut, Jesus came, stood among them, and said: Peace be with you. Then He says to Thomas: Bring your finger here and see My hands; bring your hand and put it into My side, and do not disbelieve, but believe. Thomas answered Him: My Lord and my God. Jesus said to him: Because you have seen Me, Thomas, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed. In the sight of His disciples, Jesus indeed performed many other signs, which are not written in this book. But these have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that, believing, you may have life in His name.

a.g: the first day of the week

ex.w065: Insufflavit describes Jesus’ act of breathing in the presence of the disciples. The Latin sentence does not separately say “on them”. The direction of the gesture is supplied by the context.
ex.w181: Here fidelis contrasts with incredulus, “unbelieving”. It means believing or having faith, rather than merely being reliable.
